# ECN-2026-039 - Change notice - Hot Forge induction billet heater #2

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P2, line P2-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L1-IH02

Reason for change
-----------------
Background: Operational trends and maintenance logs showed recurring thermal cycling events and longer cool-down periods on EQ-P2-L1-IH02. Investigation identified that coil cooling water flow was operating at or just below acceptable thresholds for prolonged periods during heavy duty cycles. Although no immediate damage was observed, risk analysis determined that ensuring a higher minimum flow reduces coil insulation stress, prevents localized overheating, and extends coil life. This ECN formalizes an update to the documented minimum coil cooling water flow requirement for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 and defines implementation and verification steps.

Root cause: Flow variability combined with marginal setpoints on flow monitoring allowed transient low-flow conditions to persist. Contributing factors included control hysteresis and intermittent valve stiction that were not captured under the prior preventive maintenance scheme. The change addresses the detection and control of flow to reduce risk of premature coil failure and unplanned downtime.

Change summary: The coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 55 L/min. This ECN updates operational limits, inspection criteria, and maintenance task acceptance to align documentation, control setpoints, and maintenance practices with the new minimum flow requirement.

Affected items
--------------
- Equipment: EQ-P2-L1-IH02 mechanical cooling circuit, flow sensor, control valve, and associated interlock logic.
- Documentation revisions: Update MM-P2-L1-IH02 to reflect the new flow minimum in the mechanical maintenance procedures; update SOP-P2-L1-04 to include operational verification steps for the cooling circuit; update control narrative and tuning notes as required in MM-P2-L1-IH02.
- Process and quality checks: Update QS-PROC-06 references where part temperature stability criteria depend on coil thermal control.
- Spare parts: Any flow sensor or valve replacements must be checked against the updated acceptance criteria defined in MM-P2-L1-IH02.

Implementation
--------------
Scope: Implementation covers adjustment of control setpoints, calibration and testing of flow metering, validation of alarms and interlocks, and updates to preventive maintenance and operating procedures. The coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 55 L/min. All systems and documents listed under Affected items must be completed prior to returning the induction heater to full production.

Steps:
- Update the PLC setpoint and alarm thresholds to enforce the new minimum flow requirement for EQ-P2-L1-IH02. Ensure alarm behavior is consistent with QS-PROC-06 requirements for process interruptions.
- Calibrate the flow sensor in place and bench-check spare sensors according to MM-P2-L1-IH02 calibration steps. Record calibration results and calibration certificate reference in the maintenance log.
- Replace or refurbish the control valve if mechanical inspection reveals sticking or drift beyond the acceptance criteria in MM-P2-L1-IH02. Validate valve travel and response under simulated loads.
- Implement a verification procedure in SOP-P2-L1-04 for operators to confirm coil cooling water flow meets the stated minimum prior to heater startup and during shift handovers. Include guidance for immediate actions on alarm and escalation to maintenance.
- Perform a validation run sequence to demonstrate stable operation with the new minimum flow. Log flow readings and control responses to show compliance during representative operating conditions.

Examples of actions:
- Example operator check: confirm display reading and alarm status as documented in SOP-P2-L1-04 before initiating a billet heat cycle for EQ-P2-L1-IH02.
- Example maintenance check: record post-calibration flow reading and attach calibration sticker to the flow meter housing per MM-P2-L1-IH02.

Records to keep
---------------
- Calibration certificate for flow sensor with signature and location reference recorded in the equipment file for EQ-P2-L1-IH02.
- Commissioning and validation report demonstrating that EQ-P2-L1-IH02 maintains the coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 55 L/min during test scenarios. Include raw logs and trending graphs archived in the department document control system.
- Revised procedure pages from MM-P2-L1-IH02 and SOP-P2-L1-04 showing redline and final text. Maintain change rationale archive and approval record.
- Alarm log extract showing historical occurrences and post-implementation suppression or elimination of low-flow events.
- Training records indicating personnel briefed on revisions to SOP-P2-L1-04 and any new operator checks related to cooling flow.

Rationale and expected outcome
------------------------------
Maintaining the coil cooling water flow at or above the stated minimum will reduce thermal stress on coil insulation, lower the probability of localized coil hot spots, and improve overall heater reliability. Alignment of control setpoints, sensor accuracy, and maintenance acceptance criteria will reduce unplanned outages and support quality stability for parts processed on line P2-L1 in the Hot Forge cell. This change is preventive in nature and intended to extend mean time between coil interventions.

References
----------
- MM-P2-L1-IH02
- QS-PROC-06
- SOP-P2-L1-04

Approvals
---------
Engineering approval, maintenance oversight, operations acceptance, and quality concurrence are required to close this ECN. Signatures and dates will be recorded in the document control system upon acceptance. Implementation shall not proceed past initial calibration steps until approvals are logged against this ECN record.

Contact
-------
For implementation coordination and to request copies of revised procedure pages, contact the plant engineering lead listed in the EQ-P2-L1-IH02 equipment file.
